correctness.rationale: The weighted forest determinant is proved via an augmented vertex and the matrix-tree theorem with valid signed polynomial substitution. The exact determinant of K_{m,n} is obtained by a block Schur complement with positive diagonal factors for all m,n>=2. Walsh diagonalization yields exact multiplicities. For even-even shores, parity precludes zeros. For odd balanced shores, writing deviations about the midpoint shows any noncentral product zero would require Q(a-b)=2ab with Q(a-b)>=Q>2ab. For adjacent shores, the unique candidate is isolated by 0<u-v<1, impossible for integers, using a strict quadratic bound for all d>=2. Direct independent forest enumeration, exact Walsh transforms and integer Bareiss determinants plus dimension sweeps pass 33444 assertions; the finite checks do not replace the all-order proof.

originality.rationale: The exact two-shore root enumerator and general matrix-forest identity are classical and credited. What is assessed is the Walsh-character zero locus and the all-size uniqueness proofs: central binomial square nullity for odd balanced shores, no zeros for even-even shores, and a unique zero for every consecutive-shore graph. The inspected Jin–Liu and Székely primary texts derive root counts, not Fourier inertia or this parity-sharp rank classification. The Chebotarev–Shamis determinant theorem supplies a key premise but not these arithmetic conclusions. Indexed published Fourier work on related graphs/coordinates did not establish an implication covering this theorem. Residual priority risk is retained explicitly.
residual_risks: The complete unsigned root-count formula in Jin–Liu (2004) algebraically determines the Fourier transform; the new classification may be considered a derived corollary rather than a separate result by future reviewers.
A prior unindexed signed-root generating function or analogous arithmetic argument could already give the same odd-balanced and consecutive-shore zero classifications.
Unreviewed sources may contain an equivalent rank classification; no claim of exhaustive historical priority or independent validation is made.

value.rationale: The root set of a uniformly sampled spanning rooted forest is a canonical dependent vertex-set statistic. Fourier zeros determine whether arbitrary signals can be recovered from its XOR-convolution. The result gives sharp infinite-family rank transitions: zero loss for even-balanced bicliques, exactly central-binomial-squared loss for odd-balanced bicliques with vanishing relative proportion 2/(pi*d), and exactly a single lost mode for adjacent shores. These are complete naturally parameterized classifications and are not small numerical exceptions or arbitrary parameter slices.
